title: Camp 4 close: you read it
hook: 26 chapters, 423 verses: one whole book of the Buddha's sayings

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Gandhari Dharmapada, and your line: who else carried it. Today, the end of the week, and the last day of camp four.

A copy of the Dhammapada can sit on a shelf for years, next to the other books someone means to read someday. A verse from it turns up on a poster, or a verse that was never in it at all. Reading the whole thing, in order, first verse to last, is a different matter. Seventy-four days ago, camp four began with a promise: all twenty-six chapters, all four hundred twenty-three verses, a few a day. You kept it.
screen: `A COPY ON THE SHELF.` → `A VERSE ON A POSTER.` → `SEVENTY-FIVE DAYS, KEPT.`

segments.voice: The camp's words. Dhammapada: dhamma, the teaching, and pada, a step, a path, a line of verse. Appamada: earnestness, heedfulness, the path to the deathless. Citta: the mind, trembling like a fish on dry land, straightened like an arrow. Pandita: the wise one; someone who points out your faults is like a guide to buried treasure. Arahant: the one whose path, like a bird's in the sky, can't be traced. Tanha: thirst, the creeper that grows while no one watches. Bhikkhu: the monk who lives on what is given, restrained in every sense. And brahmana: a title earned not by birth, but by conduct. Around those words, twenty-six chapters of pictures: the wheel following the ox, the island no flood can overwhelm, the spoon and the soup, the deep lake, the broken gong, the yellow leaf, the forest, the elephant, the emptied boat, the lotus leaf. Not a summary, not a quote on a mug: the book itself, in its own order. And it ends where it began. Verse one, in Max Müller's English: "All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts." Heard after four hundred twenty-two more verses, it may sound different. By now the book has shown what it means by thought: the mind that can be guarded, trained, emptied, and set free. Tomorrow camp five begins: the depths. It opens with four rooms the Buddha said a person can live in: kindness, compassion, joy for others, and equanimity. Then the foundations of mindfulness, the Heart Sutra, the koans, and more.
screen: `EIGHT WORDS, DHAMMAPADA TO BRAHMANA.` · `TWENTY-SIX CHAPTERS OF PICTURES.` · `THE BOOK ITSELF, IN ITS OWN ORDER.` · `VERSE ONE, HEARD AGAIN.` · then, large: `YOU ACTUALLY READ IT.`

segments.voice: You met verse one about ten weeks ago; let it come back now, slowly, one phrase per breath: all that we are, is the result of what we have thought, founded on our thoughts, made up of our thoughts. Then let the words go and watch the thoughts themselves for a while, arriving and leaving, the raw material the whole book was about. No need to change them; just see them.
Appamada. Earnestness, heedfulness, the path to the deathless: today the book closes, twenty-six chapters, four hundred twenty-three verses, one whole book of the Buddha's sayings, read in order.
Your line: you actually read it. All of it, every verse, in order. Camp four, complete.

screen: `DAY 231 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: FOUR ROOMS TO LIVE IN.`

howItsDone: In Theravada countries, reading or chanting the whole Dhammapada is a respected practice, some monastic students memorize it, and lay Buddhists return to it through their lives, reading a verse or a chapter at a time.
